question: Which independently consumed entrypoints justify their distribution boundary, and which facades or optional-dependency boundaries can disappear?
trigger: next returned the plate-core unit after the reads close on 2026-10-05. The ledger marked the 2026-10-04 Pursue stale because three method files and four vision files changed, and the owner's go on the pick page chose a fresh review.
requirements: Plate apps install and import platejs only; dedicated raw proof apps import plitejs (VISION.md:44).
plitejs stays an independent raw distribution (VISION.md:43).
Public roots expose author contracts, and neither distribution exposes an internal, unsafe or generic framework escape path (VISION.md:131, docs/vision/plite.md:77).
Primary-root APIs expose no public main key (VISION.md:101).
Plate re-exports the approved Plite surface by identity (VISION.md:134), which the release check enforces.
Optional framework or runtime peers stay behind explicit subpaths with packed runtime and declaration closure (docs/vision/common.md:152-154).
Keep the CLI schema-contract tooling and the detached compiler workflow.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 2026-10-04 audit's consumer-class reading and its rejected lanes after rechecking them, and the 2026-09-12 review's rejection of merging the distributions. Replaced the audit's @internal count, which parsed only direct re-exports with an adjacent JSDoc block, with a TypeScript 6.0.2 compiler census of every public plitejs and platejs entrypoint that resolves each alias to its declaration. Rechecked the cited doctrine lines, which moved but read the same apart from the bridge type's rename to PluginTypeProvider. No earlier test receipt is reused.
summary: The plitejs root, which platejs re-exports to every Plate app, publishes framework hooks with no author job. The compiler census finds 28 root exports tagged @internal (16 values, 12 types); plitejs/react re-exports the whole root (packages/plitejs/src/react/index.ts:1) and adds setDOMTextSyncRendererCapability; the platejs root and platejs/react carry the same 28. Six untagged root values have no docs page, no www use and no caller outside Plate's facade and source: runTrustedUpdate, MAIN_ROOT_KEY, repairEditorValue, setEditorMaxLength, reportEditorLifecycleError and withTransactionSpecDraftRead. That breaks VISION.md:101, VISION.md:131 and docs/vision/plite.md:77. The audit's guard keyed on @internal tags would miss the untagged hooks, so this review supersedes its target. Each export is classified by its job, and framework hooks are exported only from plitejs/internal. plitejs/internal and every public plitejs entrypoint share no name, so a mechanical check needs no tags, and packages/platejs/src/facade.ts imports hooks only from the bridge. Types stay public while public declarations name them. Hooks with a real app or tool use stay public or get a public replacement, such as getEditorRuntimeOwner in copied registry UI and the CLI schema-contract readers. Root doctrine states the one bridge, because VISION.md:131 and docs/vision/common.md:157 forbid any public internal entrypoint while docs/vision/plite.md:73 and :92 use plitejs/internal.

callSites.current: packages/platejs/src/facade.ts:1-49 exports initializePlugins as initializeRuntimePlugins, MAIN_ROOT_KEY, runTrustedUpdate and setEditorTransactionViewTransform from 'plitejs', and in any Plate app import { runTrustedUpdate } from 'platejs' resolves through packages/platejs/src/core.tsx:3.
callSites.proposed: packages/platejs/src/facade.ts exports the same names from 'plitejs/internal'; import { runTrustedUpdate } from 'platejs' no longer resolves in apps, while import { ElementApi, NodeApi } from 'platejs' is unchanged.

reconciliation.reason: Its Pursue holds and its rejected lanes still lose, but its target and guard keyed on @internal tags miss six untagged facade-only hooks and the plitejs/react copy of the root; the target moves to job-based classification with a disjoint bridge.

alternatives: Keeping the current design loses: both public roots keep publishing hooks with no author job, against VISION.md:101, VISION.md:131 and docs/vision/plite.md:77.

The 2026-10-04 target, which moves the tagged values and guards by tag, loses to this one: it leaves runTrustedUpdate, MAIN_ROOT_KEY and four more untagged hooks public, and its guard trusts every author to tag.
Moving hooks by job, making plitejs/internal and the public entrypoints disjoint, and stating the bridge once in root doctrine is selected. It deletes public exports and adds no runtime work.

Stripping @internal from published declarations, as ProseMirror and CodeMirror do, loses: the runtime exports stay, export * from 'plitejs' still mirrors them into platejs, and Plate's facade still needs their types.

Replacing export * from 'plitejs' in packages/platejs/src/core.tsx with a curated list loses: the release check proves facade identity over the whole Plite root, and a hand-kept list moves the sync work into Plate instead of cleaning the root.

Deleting plitejs/internal, merging the distributions, or hiding the hooks behind a symbol-keyed registry loses. VISION.md:43-44 keeps plitejs an independent raw distribution, two npm packages cannot share private module state without one channel, and a hidden registry is the same channel without types or a name.
For the scale gate, this is an export-only cut with unchanged runtime work, so no benchmark lane applies.
proofLimits: The census read declarations through the TypeScript compiler and ran nothing else: no build, typecheck, test, packed release or browser. Consumer counts are word searches over content/docs, apps/www/src without generated files, packages, benchmarks and the vision files, so a generic name can collide; only the borderline values were read at their call sites. Whether the 12 tagged types can leave the root depends on whether public declarations name them, which the plan must check against built declarations. The doctrine conflict is named, not resolved. dispatchCommand, evaluateCommand and probeCommandNativeEquivalent also belong to the closed commands scope. The census ran on 477da4cf9a with no uncommitted edits under packages/plitejs/src or packages/platejs/src. Other editors were read from local clones and not built.
